cells.date: 1646 (completed by the Westminster Assembly; approved by the Church of Scotland 1647)
cells.excerpt: This effectual call is of God's free and special grace alone, not from anything at all foreseen in man, who is altogether passive therein
cells.shows: The Confession teaches that the sinner is altogether passive in effectual calling and answers the call only after the Spirit has renewed him.

cells.section: Third and Fourth Main Points of Doctrine, Article 12 (Regeneration a Supernatural Work)
cells.excerpt: the making alive so clearly proclaimed in the Scriptures, which God works in us without our help
cells.shows: The continental Reformed standard says regeneration is worked by God without human help and does not leave it in human power whether to be converted.

cells.section: Chapter 29, Of the Lord's Supper, section 7
cells.excerpt: do then also, inwardly by faith, really and indeed, yet not carnally and corporally but spiritually, receive, and feed upon, Christ crucified, and all benefits of his death
cells.shows: Worthy receivers really feed on Christ in the Supper, spiritually and by faith, while the Confession denies that his body is corporally in, with or under the elements.

cells.excerpt: the grace promised is not only offered, but really exhibited, and conferred, by the Holy Ghost, to such (whether of age or infants) as that grace belongeth unto
cells.shows: Baptism, including infant baptism, is a means by which the Holy Ghost really confers the promised grace on those to whom it belongs, in God's appointed time.

cells.section: Chapter 1, Of the Holy Scripture, section 1 (see also section 6: nothing to be added 'whether by new revelations of the Spirit, or traditions of men')
cells.excerpt: which maketh the Holy Scripture to be most necessary; those former ways of God's revealing his will unto his people being now ceased
cells.shows: The Confession says God's former ways of revealing his will have ceased now that revelation is committed to writing; it does not name tongues or healing.

cells.section: Chapter 7, Of God's Covenant with Man, section 6 (see also Chapter 25, section 2: the visible church 'is the kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ')
cells.excerpt: There are not therefore two covenants of grace, differing in substance, but one and the same, under various dispensations.
cells.shows: One covenant of grace runs through both testaments, given under the gospel to all nations, both Jews and Gentiles, and the visible church is called Christ's kingdom.

cells.section: Chapter 1, Of the Holy Scripture, section 10
cells.excerpt: The supreme judge by which all controversies of religion are to be determined ... can be no other but the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture.
cells.shows: Decrees of councils and opinions of ancient writers are all to be examined by Scripture, which is the supreme judge of every controversy.

cells.section: Chapter 31, Of Synods and Councils, section 3 in the American text opened (section 4 in the original 1646 numbering)
cells.excerpt: All synods or councils, since the Apostles' times, whether general or particular, may err; and many have erred. Therefore they are not to be made the rule of faith
cells.shows: Councils may err and are a help, not the rule of faith; this matches the subordinate-but-real authority that keeps the coordinate short of 100.

cells.document: The Directory for the Publick Worship of God
cells.date: 1645 (Westminster Assembly; adopted by the Church of Scotland General Assembly, February 1645)
cells.excerpt: resolved to lay aside the former Liturgy, with the many rites and ceremonies formerly used in the worship of God; and have agreed upon this following Directory
cells.shows: The Assembly set aside the Book of Common Prayer's fixed liturgy and replaced it with a directory giving the general heads and order of worship, leaving the wording of prayers to the minister.
cells.binding: Historic standard. Binding status varies today: American Presbyterian bodies (OPC, PCA) use their own later directories for worship, and parts of those are advisory rather than constitutional.

cells.section: Chapter 21, Of Religious Worship, and the Sabbath Day, section 1
cells.excerpt: the acceptable way of worshiping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited by his own revealed will
cells.shows: Worship may include only what Scripture prescribes (the regulative principle); this is the reason given for dropping ceremonies, but by itself it does not settle set forms versus free prayer.

notes: All excerpts were copied from the pages listed, fetched on 2026-09-19; curly apostrophes on the source pages are written here as straight apostrophes, and the authority 1.10 excerpt uses an ellipsis for an omitted middle clause (the full sentence is on the page). The opc.org text is the Orthodox Presbyterian Church's edition of the Confession, which carries the American revisions (1788 and later) to chapters 20, 23, 25 and 31; none of the sections quoted here except the numbering of chapter 31 is affected by those revisions, but anyone citing 'WCF 31.4' from the 1646 text should know it is 31.3 on the page opened. The Canons of Dort excerpt is from the Christian Reformed Church's 2011 English translation, which is in copyright, so it is kept under 20 words and marked link only; the Latin original of 1619 is public domain. Gifts: WCF 1.1 and 1.6 are the passages confessional Presbyterians themselves cite for cessationism, but they speak of revelation ceasing and do not mention tongues, prophecy or healing by name; the coordinate of 90 rests on how the tradition reads those sections, and no denominational study report was opened for this file. Kingdom: the Confession predates dispensationalism, so it states the one-covenant, one-people position positively rather than rejecting the rival view by name; no document rejecting dispensationalism by name was opened. Worship: the coordinate of 67 (leaning free, not fully free) fits the Directory well, which abolishes a prescribed liturgy yet fixes the parts and order of the service; the continental Reformed churches of the same family historically kept set liturgical forms (not opened or cited here), which is a further reason the coordinate sits well short of 100. No cell points against the audited coordinate.
